location: Location unknown — studio real-photo postcard, ‘A Canyon Baby’
recipient: Mrs. J.A. Murray, Cambridge Springs, R.D. #3, Pennsylvania
notes: Front: sepia real-photo postcard of a young bear cub among tall pines, captioned in white ink ‘A Canyon Baby’ with a photographer/studio credit below that’s not fully legible [best guess: something like ‘Caukins’]. 2¢ John Adams stamp. Message: “Tues. Dear Florence, We just received a card D. They are coming up this week, so I don't know what to tell you about Sun. We were planning to come until the card came. I think it will be better to wait until later to come. Sorry! But think that will be best.”

location: Kansas City, Missouri — First Congregational Church
address: Admiral Blvd. & Highland Ave., Kansas City, MO
year: August 1959 (postmark day illegible, town name also only partly legible — ends in ‘-tonsburg,’ MO)
recipient: Mrs. M.R.C. Pomeroy [best guess on surname], Sturgis(?), Colorado
notes: Front: color postcard of the Gothic-style First Congregational Church with vintage automobiles parked out front. Fab. by Max Bernstein, Kansas City, Mo. Card #13476. 1¢ green Franklin stamp. Address and message are both written sideways/rotated on the card, and the message is cut off at the visible edge. Message: “Sun. Dear [name unclear], we are feeling fine, sure are having a fine time such a nice visit. Every thing looks so good. The weather is fine. Hope you are all well and that [Jack?]… Myriam”

address: Mission Motel, Mission, South Dakota — junction of U.S. 18 & 83, Rosebud Indian Reservation
recipient: Mr. J.S. Bennett, 1122 Prospect, Kansas City, Mo.
notes: Front: color photo of the Mission Motel building with 'MOTEL' sign. Caption: ‘Located in the heart of the Rosebud Indian Reservation, at the junction of the Chicago Black Hills Highway U.S. 18 and 83… Sixteen Units, each with Private Shower Bath — Good Beds — Close to Cafe — Open Year Around — 24 Hour Service.’ Pub. by Pospeshil Photographers, Sioux City, Iowa. 3¢ Statue of Liberty stamp. Message: “Mon. 17th. Dear Father; We are on our way back to Lincoln — I don't know what day I'll get home, but soon I guess. Hope you are well, Bernice.”

location: Oberammergau, Bavaria, Germany — Passionsspieldorf (Passion Play Village)
year: Letter dated June 18, 1965 (Bad [town name uncertain] 18.6.65); postmarked/annotated 7.7.65
recipient: Albert [surname uncertain, cursive — reads like ‘Hincke’], 509 Avenue of the Oaks, Houston 22, Texas 77009, USA
notes: Front: four-panel color postcard of Oberammergau — the Passion Play theater, a painted Lüftlmalerei house with the onion-domed church tower, a fully frescoed Bavarian house, and a cable car over the Alps. Publisher Schöning & Co., Lübeck (Farbkarte). Translation: “Dear Albert! We congratulate you most warmly on your 66th birthday, wishing you good health and God's blessing. With best regards, Alwin, Käthe and Gerda.” Message in German: “Lieber Albert! Wir gratulieren recht herzlich zu Deinem 66.ten Geburtstag, wünschen Dir gute Gesundheit u. Gottes Segen. Mit besten Grüßen, Alwin, Käthe u. Gerda.”

location: Mt. Baker National Forest, Washington — Mount Shuksan reflected in Picture Lake
address: Near Mt. Baker Lodge, Mt. Baker National Forest, Washington
recipient: Dr. & Mrs. E.P. Evans, 120 West 10th, Loveland, Colorado 80537
notes: Front: Ektachrome by J. Boyd Ellis, published by Ellis Post Card Co., Arlington, WA. Caption: ‘Mount Shuksan in Mt. Baker National Forest located in northwest Washington… taken from near Mt. Baker Lodge.’ 8¢ Einstein stamp. Message: “June 9-71. Dear sis & Bro — all well here & sure pretty. Louise said you should be sure and fish. We've sent all his friends & renter a card — Ann called yest a.m. Jim & Steve both working at Parsons — write us & take care. Love, Louis & Jean & All.”
